result:
`scripts/backup.sh --dry-run SOURCE DEST` now lists every path under SOURCE, prints `would back up SOURCE to DEST/<date>`, and exits without creating or copying anything. The README usage and options line match. I ran both modes against a temp directory: the dry run left DEST uncreated and the normal run still copies.

```sh
dry=
if [ "${1:-}" = --dry-run ]; then dry=1; shift; fi
src=${1:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
dest=${2:?usage: backup.sh [--dry-run] SOURCE DEST}
target=$dest/$(date +%F)
if [ -n "$dry" ]; then
    find "$src" ! -path "$src"
    echo "would back up $src to $target"
    exit 0
fi
```

`--dry-run` must come first; it is not recognised after SOURCE or DEST.
